title: essun profile artifact (design doc D2, ladder S3)
description: The versioned profile format: a profile is a first-class, engine-separable artifact carrying ten required elements (design doc D2, docs/plans/design-integration-20261029.md): source identity/revision, provenance and permissions, interpreted requirements WITH dispositions (D1), declared implementation freedom, backend capability bindings, executable checks, supported workloads/observables, calibration scope, known omissions, and versioning rules — plus the two identity keys 'format' and 'profile_id'. DRAFT CONTRACT: not promoted by an ADR; the format carries its own version (format.version) and every change to it is a versioned, conscious change. Structural rules live here; cross-reference rules (bindings/checks must reference existing requirement ids; simulated_behavior requires a binding; conformance_test requires a check; calibration status/target consistency) are enforced by the loader (essun.specir.profile_format) and pinned in agreement with this schema by tests/specir/test_profile_format.py.

format.description: Identity of the FORMAT itself (the artifact is self-describing; the loader dispatches on it). While the format is a 0.x draft, loader and artifact must agree exactly on version.

profile_id.description: Stable identity of this profile artifact (e.g. 'uec-1.1-semantic'). Comparisons are of named profiles.

source.description: Element 1: source identity/revision — which standard/document the profile interprets.

provenance.description: Element 2: provenance and permissions — the repo-level license-gate source record and access status. License review precedes ingestion; the profile never carries restricted text.

access.description: Access class of the source record (e.g. PUBLIC_READ, APPROVAL_REQUIRED), copied verbatim from the license-gate registry row.

requirements.description: Element 3: interpreted requirements WITH dispositions (D1). An empty object set is allowed only as a VISIBLE absence: requirements.note is then required.

freedom.description: Element 4: declared implementation freedom — degrees of freedom the source explicitly leaves open. Never invent normative values; use a free parameter.

bindings.description: Element 5: backend capability bindings — which requirement (disposition simulated_behavior) is executed by which backend capability. Enforced cross-reference: a binding must name an existing simulated_behavior requirement. May be empty: a profile executed by no backend today says so by having no bindings, never by omitting the element.

checks.description: Element 6: executable checks — golden/negative/invariant checks exercising the profile's requirements. Every conformance_test requirement must be referenced by at least one check. May be empty.

supported.description: Element 7: supported workloads and observables — the profile's declared executable surface.

calibration.description: Element 8: calibration scope — verification != calibration (hard rule 5); a profile states what it is calibrated against, or says uncalibrated.

targets.description: Anchor ids or dataset identities the calibration used; must be empty exactly when status is uncalibrated.

omissions.description: Element 9: known omissions — what the profile does NOT interpret or execute, stated visibly (honesty over coverage).

versioning.description: Element 10: versioning rules — the PROFILE's own version (independent of format.version) and the declared change policy: which changes bump which component. Anchor citations are immutable: a changed citation is a new version, never a silent edit.

requirement.description: One interpreted requirement. Extra keys (keyword, subject, unit, value_kind, ...) are preserved for the migrating profile families.

anchor_ids.description: Every standard-derived value keeps a source anchor; anchor ids resolve against the profile's registry (checked explicitly via check_anchor_refs — never at load, so the artifact stays engine/placement independent).

disposition.description: D1 disposition: how the platform executes this requirement. unsupported is a valid, visible answer.

capability.description: Name inside the backend's declared CAPABILITIES (the dict every essun backend publishes). Unsupported bindings fail loudly via check_bindings_against — never silently approximated.
